clue.text: Olympic ski resort needs referee

definitions.meaning: the Canadian resort in British Columbia that hosted alpine events at the 2010 Winter Games
a match official, so called from the instrument he blows to stop play

explanation.surface: A ski resort hosting the Olympics must find someone to officiate.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a named Canadian ski town, and one who blows the whistle, i.e. a sports official.

clue.text: Oil Homer represented as something passed on

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are presented again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Homer's oil, painted or depicted, becomes a family legacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like a poet or cartoon father but is just letters: OIL HOMER rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A family treasure handed down through generations is something passed on.

clue.text: Radio with headphones is to cause disagreement

parts.note: a radio is a set, a receiving apparatus
headphones are worn by (beside) the ears

explanation.surface: Someone claims a radio listened to through headphones causes arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'set by the ears' means to make people quarrel; the wordplay reads it literally as a radio set held by one's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stir up strife between people, i.e. provoke a quarrel.

clue.text: Dressing covering, disabled connective tissue

indicators.note: the dressing wraps around the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds
game, as in a game leg, means lame or crippled

explanation.surface: A wound dressing is wrapped over a crippled body's connective tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' meaning lame (a 'game leg') is an old-fashioned sense solvers may not know; 'covering' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: This band of fibrous tissue connects bones at a joint.

clue.text: Garden feature seen in China but not its capital

indicators.note: its capital is the capital (first) letter of the word, here dropped

parts.note: china is porcelain tableware, i.e. crockery

explanation.surface: A garden feature is seen in China but not in Beijing.
explanation.walkthrough: China with its capital looks like the country and Beijing; it is porcelain, CROCKERY, losing its capital letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock garden, an arrangement of stones and alpine plants, is a garden feature.

clue.text: One of the big guns making a name in the law

indicators.note: the letter for name is placed inside the word for law

parts.note: a canon is a law or rule, especially of the church
N is a standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: One of the top people makes a reputation in the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big guns' reads as important people, but it is literal artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A large piece of artillery is literally one of the big guns.

clue.text: Very probably a source of supply

definitions.meaning: as in 'it may ... rain': quite likely
a shaft sunk for water or oil, figuratively any resource

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the adverb used in 'may well happen', and a spring or shaft providing water or oil.

clue.text: Penny and Rae rambling in the mountains

indicators.note: the letters wander about like walkers rambling, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Penny and Rae are out hiking in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the adjective for the range on the French-Spanish border, so 'in the mountains' defines it adjectivally.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things in the range of peaks on the French-Spanish border.

clue.text: Soldiers endued with temper ultimately qualify for the glasshouse

parts.note: OR is other ranks, i.e. ordinary soldiers
temper as rage, i.e. anger

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Soldiers with a temper end up qualifying for the glasshouse, a military prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The glasshouse' is British slang for a military prison, which suits the soldiers; here it is a literal glass building for growing citrus.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatory originally for growing citrus trees is a kind of glasshouse.

clue.text: Give ear to band record

definitions.meaning: an archaic verb meaning to listen
a strip of cloth such as a selvage edge
a written catalogue or register of items

explanation.definitionFit: Triple definition: archaic for listen, a narrow strip or border, and a catalogue of items.

clue.text: Livid, in distress, Alban buckled

indicators.note: the letters are in a distressed, disordered state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alban, upset after his bicycle wheel buckled, is livid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Livid' looks like angry but means bruise-coloured; 'buckled' is fodder, not the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid originally means bruise-coloured, bluish-grey, the colour of a beaten body.

clue.text: Lepidopterist helping to make connections?

definitions.meaning: someone mad about moths and similar insects: an enthusiast or nut for them
a wing-shaped threaded fastener used to join parts

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a winged fastener, and humorously a fan of winged insects.

clue.text: Preserve one's nerve

definitions.meaning: to put fruit in jars to keep it

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: to preserve food in jars, and British slang for courage or nerve.

clue.text: Call time — express regret, and make it sound right

parts.note: to call someone on the phone is to ring them
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone calls closing time, apologises, and makes it all sound convincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call time' suggests last orders in a pub; it is RING plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a statement that seems genuine, i.e. sounds right.

clue.text: When law is suspended, little woman secures cosy little home

indicators.note: the name holds the next piece safely inside it

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in the novel Little Women
a nest is a snug small dwelling

explanation.surface: A small woman holds on to her snug little house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' looks like a wife; it points to Amy from 'Little Women'.
explanation.definitionFit: A general pardon is an occasion when the law's penalties are suspended.

clue.text: Don't start to lavish praise on a place —— the cheek of it!

indicators.note: the word's first letter is not allowed to begin it

parts.note: to laud is to praise lavishly
a city is a place

explanation.surface: Stop heaping praise on some town: what nerve!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' drops the first letter from LAUD to leave AUD; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacity means impudence or nerve, the kind of cheek one exclaims at.

clue.text: Old soldier in TA never discharged

indicators.note: the letters are dismissed from their order, like a soldier leaving the ranks

explanation.surface: An old soldier who served in the Territorial Army was never discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force, which suits the surface; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-serviceman with long experience is an old soldier.

clue.text: Full of expectation, choose a portion of Asian staple

parts.note: to elect is to choose

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, its last letter lost

parts.note: rice is the staple food of much of Asia

explanation.surface: Excited, someone picks a helping of rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A portion of' asks for part of RICE, losing its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric atmosphere is charged and thrilling, full of expectation.

clue.text: A forebear, a wise old man who went round clubs

indicators.note: the old man surrounds the next piece

parts.note: Nestor is the aged counsellor in Homer's Iliad
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: An ancestor was a sage who went from club to club.
explanation.walkthrough: NESTOR is the wise elder of Greek legend; 'who went round' puts C inside him, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a person from whom one descends, i.e. a forebear.

clue.text: Approximate weight about to be worked

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes around the other word

parts.note: a rough estimate is approximate

explanation.surface: An approximate weight is about to be worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' signals a container here, not a reversal; 'to be' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrought is an old past participle of work, as in wrought iron.

clue.text: Girl's bloomer results in catastrophe

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and the possessive gives Di's
an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A girl's blunder leads to calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a mistake, which fits the catastrophe; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, a synonym for catastrophe.

clue.text: Magnate not coy, by any means

indicators.note: the letters may be arranged in any way at all

explanation.surface: A business magnate is not at all shy.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT COY rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy powerful businessperson, a synonym for magnate.

clue.text: Remove all traces of a sequence of notes

definitions.meaning: to wipe out or erase completely
every letter is a musical note name, A to G

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: to erase, and a string of letters that are all musical note names.

clue.text: Angry people skiing

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a country is a nation, a people

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered people are out skiing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skiing' alone defines the answer as the long-distance kind of skiing over open land.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-country is a form of skiing over level open terrain.

clue.text: Just one nursery lets youngsters put their heads together

indicators.note: the first letters (heads) of four words are joined

explanation.surface: A nursery allows children to collaborate, just this once.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'one nursery lets youngsters' make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Only means merely or solely, as just does.

clue.text: Attention held by piano teacher

indicators.note: the answer is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A piano teacher demands attention.
explanation.walkthrough: pia-NO TE-acher holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Note means notice or attention, as in 'take note'.

clue.text: Henry, in addition to Mark, sent back to Scottish prison

indicators.note: the whole run of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance
too means also
a blot is a mark or stain

explanation.surface: Henry and Mark are sent back to a Scottish jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' turns H + TOO + BLOT end to end. A tolbooth was a Scottish town hall, often with a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the old town hall held the burgh jail, so the word means a prison there.

clue.text: One pet about to become uncommunicative

indicators.note: the words for one and pet are turned round together

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a cat is a pet
to turn is to become, as in turn sour

explanation.surface: A pet is about to stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reverses the pair I + CAT to give TACI; it is not a container here.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means reserved and saying little, i.e. uncommunicative.
